name: arg2p
description: Structured argumentation in Prolog: write theories (ASPIC+, ABA, abstract frameworks), see their errors as you type, solve queries and browse their argument graphs.
author: Giuseppe Pisano

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The Java running the language server and its options are set in the user settings alone, never by a workspace.

arg2p.java.path.markdownDescription: The `java` running the language server, in the user settings alone (a workspace cannot run a program of its own). Empty: the Java runtime the extension bundles, or else the one of `JAVA_HOME`, or else `java` on the path (21 or later).

arg2p.java.options.markdownDescription: The options of the JVM running the language server: `-Xmx8g`, say, for the heap of large graphs. Resolution goes deep: keep a large stack (`-Xss512m`).

arg2p.flags.markdownDescription: The flags a theory is first solved with, as Prolog facts (the solver keeps those of each theory afterwards).

enumDescriptions: Beside the theory, on its right
Under the theory, in a group of editors of its own
arg2p.solver.position.markdownDescription: Where **Arg2P: Open the Solver** opens the solver of a theory.

arg2p.federation.enabled.markdownDescription: Whether the language server federates with those of the devices nearby (the VS Code of the same local network) and lets phones join: each device shows its name and a 4-digit code, and links to another once its code is typed (see the view **Arg2P Federation**). Disabled, it neither listens nor is heard, and **Parallel** solves on the workers of this device alone.

arg2p.federation.name.markdownDescription: The name of this device, as the devices nearby see it. Empty: the name of the host.

scripts.verify: npm run check && npm run build && npm test && npm run test:vscode
